Whose duty is it to fix that?","fact_ids":["sec12-F02"]},"answer":{"text":"Ray's, as the driver of a rider under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-R01"]},"rationale":{"text":"Whoever drives anyone under eighteen must secure that rider in a belt, booster or child seat wherever seated.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Why and who buckles","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Belts double survival odds.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04"]},{"text":"Every seat in Virginia.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04"]},{"text":"The physician waiver.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the first lesson on seat belts, traffic stops, airbags and child seats. We start with seat belts. Buckling up doubles your odds of surviving a crash and more than doubles your odds of avoiding serious injury. Virginia requires a belt in every seat, for the driver and for all front and rear passengers, and the driver is responsible for securing any rider under eighteen. The manual also explains how a belt should be worn, including a note for expectant mothers, and it describes the one way to be excused from belting: a signed statement from a licensed physician. By the end of this lesson you should know who must buckle, how, and who can excuse it.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who must buckle","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driver plus all front and rear riders.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F01"]},{"text":"Driver secures anyone under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F01"]},{"text":"Belt, booster or child seat, wherever seated.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Virginia belts every seat. The driver and all front and rear riders must buckle. And whoever drives anyone under eighteen must secure that young rider in a belt, a booster or a child seat, wherever they are seated. So the rule covers every rider in the car, and for riders under eighteen it puts the duty on the driver. Buckling up doubles crash-survival odds and more than doubles the odds of avoiding grave injury, which is the reason the manual gives for belting. There is one way to be excused, which comes on the next slide: a physician's signed statement for a real physical or medical condition.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Wearing the belt","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lap strap low across lap and thighs.","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Shoulder strap over shoulder and chest, snug.","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R02"]},{"text":"Expectant mothers: lowest on the pelvis.","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Wear the lap strap low across the lap and thighs, and the shoulder strap over the shoulder and chest, snug. Never sling the shoulder strap behind your back or under your arm. Expectant mothers wear the lap belt lowest on the pelvis. So lap straps ride low on the thighs and shoulder straps cross the chest snugly, never behind the back or under the arm, with pregnancy belting lowest of all. A belt worn behind the back or under the arm does not follow the manual's instruction. Check both straps when you buckle: the lap strap low and snug, and the shoulder strap across your shoulder and chest.","fact_ids":["sec12-F03","sec12-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Only a doctor excuses","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Licensed physician can waive belting.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"For a physical or medical condition.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-R01"]},{"text":"Carry the signed statement.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some people think a belt can be skipped for comfort, for a short trip, or with a note from a parent. The manual allows one exception. A licensed physician can waive belting where a physical or medical condition makes it unreasonable, and the waived person must carry the signed statement naming the bearer and the reason. So belts bind the driver plus every rider, with riders under eighteen secured by the driver, while only a physician's signed waiver for a real medical cause can excuse belting. No other note or reason in the manual excuses a rider from buckling up, and the signed statement must be carried.","fact_ids":["sec12-F04","sec12-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the duty","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-R01","sec12-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driver with a sixteen-year-old cousin.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-R01","sec12-F04"]},{"text":"Cousin in back, no belt.","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-R01","sec12-F04"]},{"text":"Whose duty?","fact_ids":["sec12-F02","sec12-R01","sec12-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Ray is driving his sixteen-year-old cousin, who is sitting in the back seat without a belt. Whoever drives anyone under eighteen must secure that young rider in a belt, booster or child seat, wherever they are seated. Back-seat riders are not exempt, because Virginia belts every seat, front and rear. Only a licensed physician's signed statement, carried by the rider, could excuse belting, and only for a physical or medical condition. Virginia requires the driver and all front and rear passengers to buckle, and the driver must secure any rider under eighteen in a belt, booster or child seat. Wear the lap strap low across the lap and thighs and the shoulder strap over the shoulder and chest, snug, never behind the back or under the arm, and expectant mothers wear the belt lowest on the pelvis. Only a licensed physician can waive belting, for a physical or medical condition, and the waived person carries the signed statement.","fact_ids":["sec12-F01","sec12-F02","sec12-F03","sec12-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec12-u02","module_id":"sec12-m02","objective_ids":["sec12-u02"],"title":{"text":"Traffic stops","fact_ids":["sec12-F05","sec12-F06","sec12-R03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"When an officer flags you down, the manual lists steps for pulling over and setting up the stop.","fact_ids":["sec12-F05"]},{"text":"During the stop, posture, documents and the citation each have stated rules.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-F07","sec12-F08"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Sue is stopped by an officer and asked for her registration, which is in the glove box.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"When asked, tell the officer where the documents are and fetch them slowly with one hand still on the wheel.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07","sec12-R04"]},"result":{"text":"Sue says the registration is in the glove box, then reaches for it slowly, keeping one hand on the wheel.","fact_ids":["sec12-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking that signing a citation admits guilt.","fact_ids":["sec12-F08"]},"correction":{"text":"Signing the citation concedes no guilt, and refusing to sign risks arrest or a trip to the station; disputes belong in court.","fact_ids":["sec12-F08","sec12-R04","sec12-R05"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Hands on the wheel; argue in court.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Sue is handed a citation. It also explains what to say, where disputes belong, and what it means to sign a citation. Remain seated unless the officer asks you to step out. Turn on your hazard lights, and at night turn on the dome light. Turn off the engine, the radio and any gadgets that would block conversation. Lower the window, because the officer may come to either side of the car. So stops open with parking, flashers, the dome light and gadgets off. Note the window detail: officers may approach from the driver side or the passenger side, so the manual says to lower the window rather than assume which side the officer will come to.","fact_ids":["sec12-F05","sec12-R03","sec12-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Sitting through the stop","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Belts stay buckled for everyone.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-R03"]},{"text":"Hands visible on top of the wheel.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-R03"]},{"text":"No move that suggests hiding or grabbing.","fact_ids":["sec12-F06","sec12-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Throughout the stop, belts stay buckled for the driver and all riders. The manual sets out who can waive a child restraint and what drivers pay when a child is not properly restrained. It says where children are safest in the car, where to get a child seat installation checked, and why a child must never be held in a lap. It gives rules for doors and child locks. And it names places in a vehicle where children may never ride, including a ban on anyone under sixteen riding in a pickup bed. By the end of this lesson you should know the fines, the safest seat, and the banned riding places.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-F10","sec12-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec12-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Waivers and fines","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Physician waiver for weight, fitness or medical cause.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R06"]},{"text":"Signed statement carried by the driver.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R06"]},{"text":"First conviction: fifty; a later offense may mean five hundred.","fact_ids":["sec12-F09","sec12-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"A licensed physician may waive a child restraint for weight, physical fitness or other medical grounds. The driver transporting the child carries the signed statement, which names the child and the reason. Drivers remain responsible for proper restraints. A first conviction brings fifty dollars; a later offense may carry a five-hundred-dollar penalty. Put as a contrast: physician waivers cover weight, physical fitness or other medical grounds with a signed identifying statement carried; a first conviction brings fifty dollars and another offense may mean five hundred. So doors stay shut, locked and child-locked with full stops before opening, while seats are installed safest in the center back, with check events to verify them. Children may never ride in station wagon luggage areas or under open hatchbacks, and anyone under sixteen may never ride in a pickup bed, even beneath a camper shell. He should ride inside the cab, buckled, since Virginia belts every seat.
